rule: Elixir: guards are calls of their function. `:erlang_mod.f` and an imported Erlang module are `erlang_mod.f`.
notes: call_type convention (SPEC gives no Elixir mapping; Elixir has no methods and the `macro` type is defined only for C/C++/ObjC and Rust `name!`): every local, imported and remote call is direct, a call through a value is callback. Operators and special forms (`|>`, `=`, `case`, `fn`, `%{}`, `__MODULE__`) are language constructs, not calls. Bare Kernel functions resolve to the auto-imported Kernel (Elixir decision: 'with one import known to export the name, that import is the target'): `Kernel.<name>`, medium. Guard calls (`is_number`, `is_tuple`) are calls with the guarded function as caller, on the guard's line. `sqrt(x)` resolves through `import :math, only: [sqrt: 1]` to `math.sqrt`; `:ets.new` is `ets.new`. The `import` line is a module dependency.
